entry.title: How SmartKNN Learns Feature Weights Internally.
entry.summary:
“KNN secretly behaves like metric learning once you stop being lazy with distances.” KNN is famous for being simple. But SmartKNN flips that assumption. Instead of treating KNN as a static, distance-based dinosaur, SmartKNN treats it as a geometry problem: Before searching neighbors… what if we reshape the entire feature space itself? This article isn’t just a code explanation - it’s the underlying logic that makes SmartKNN behave like a lightweight metric-learning model. Let’s walk through how SmartKNN learns feature weights internally by analyzing the actual code that powers the system. Most models learn parameters. Each feature weight defines how much that axis matters in the distance function: distance = sqrt( Σ weight[i] * (x[i] - y[i])² )
